[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance document defines the approved programming languages for Gainwell Technologies application development, maps each language to the workload types where it is the appropriate fit, and provides teams with the information needed to make informed, fit-for-purpose language selections within the enterprise's governed polyglot model. It also communicates what enterprise tooling and support is available for each language and defines the process for languages not yet in the approved set.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

Following this guidance ensures:

- Teams select the right tool for their workload type, reducing avoidable rework and architectural debt
- Enterprise tooling, security scanning, and CI/CD pipeline support is predictable and understood before work begins
- Language selections made outside the documented polyglot set are reviewed by the Architecture Review Board before substantial investment is made
- Gaps in tooling coverage are visible and tracked rather than discovered late in delivery
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **Primary Audience**: Application Architects and Senior Engineers — use this guidance to select the right language for a given workload, platform, or architectural context
- **Secondary Audience**: Development Leads and Product Engineers — use this guidance to understand which languages are supported, what enterprise tooling is available, and when to seek architectural input
- **Platform Engineering and DevOps Teams** — use this guidance to understand which languages require Golden Path tooling, pipeline templates, and runtime support
- **Enterprise Architects** — use this guidance when reviewing architecture decisions that introduce a language into a new context or workload type

[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#applicable-scenarios]

#### Applicable Scenarios

page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#scope-boundaries]

#### Scope Boundaries

- **In Scope**: Approved language portfolio, workload fit mapping, enterprise tooling support levels, security scanning coverage, architectural review process for unsupported languages
- **Out of Scope**: Language-specific implementation standards (see per-language standards linked in each language profile); SQL and database query language governance (governed by database platform standards, not this document — note: SQL represents a significant portion of the enterprise codebase including stored procedures with business logic; SQL governance is deferred to database platform standards, not omitted); documentation markup — Markdown/Mermaid governance is addressed in repository contribution guidelines; infrastructure-as-code language standards (HCL, YAML); mobile-native language selection (Swift, Kotlin)
- **Related Guidance**: [Technology Selection Strategy](../../technology/strategy/GUID-TEC-STRAT-001-technology-selection-strategy.md), [Frontend Framework Selection Guidance](../frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md)

page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

- **C#/.NET as Primary Platform**: C# and the .NET ecosystem are the primary application development platform at Gainwell. New service development defaults to C#/.NET where workload fit supports it. Python is used for data and ML workloads; TypeScript for micro-frontend and JavaScript-ecosystem services. These languages complement C# rather than compete with it.
- **Polyglot by Design**: Gainwell intentionally operates a polyglot engineering environment. Different languages serve different purposes, and prescribing a single language across all contexts is architecturally incorrect — a data pipeline, a REST API, a micro-frontend, and a batch processing job have genuinely different runtime, tooling, and ecosystem requirements.
- **Ad Hoc Selection Risk**: Without documented standards, teams select languages ad hoc, leading to choices that lack enterprise tooling support, security scanning coverage, or available skills — all of which increase delivery risk and long-term maintenance burden.
- **Tooling Coverage Gaps**: Enterprise security scanning (SAST/SCA) and CI/CD pipeline template availability varies by language. Teams need this information before committing to a language selection, not after.
- **Regulatory Environment**: Gainwell operates in healthcare and government markets subject to HIPAA, FedRAMP, and Section 508 requirements. Security toolchain completeness is therefore a material language selection criterion, not a preference.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#strategic-alignment]

#### Strategic Alignment

This guidance supports the enterprise's AWS-based, containerized, microservice, and micro-frontend architectural strategy. Each documented language is evaluated for compatibility with:

- AWS EKS container runtimes and managed service integrations
- Microservice deployment patterns (independently deployable, domain-focused services)
- CI/CD pipeline standards (GitHub Actions-based Golden Path templates)
- HIPAA/FedRAMP security scanning and vulnerability management requirements

page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#future-state-vision]

#### Future State Vision

The enterprise's future language portfolio is governed rather than consolidated. The goal is not to reduce the number of languages in use — it is to ensure that every language in active use has clear enterprise support, tooling coverage, and workload fit documentation. Languages in the "Requires Architectural Review" tier are candidates for elevation to Conditionally Supported or Fully Supported as tooling and skills availability are confirmed.
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#core-problem]

#### Core Problem

Teams currently lack documented guidance on:

1. Which languages are approved for which workload types
2. What enterprise tooling (CI/CD templates, security scanning) is available per language
3. When they must seek architectural review before adopting a language

This leads to late-stage discovery of tooling gaps, inconsistent security scanning coverage, and support burden when languages are used outside their appropriate context.

[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#language-governance-tiers]

### Language Governance Tiers

Languages are classified into three tiers that describe the level of enterprise tooling and support available. **These tiers describe tooling availability, not language preference. All languages in the approved polyglot set are valid choices for their documented workload types.**

| Tier | Label | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | **Fully Supported** | *Target state — no languages currently qualify.* Language has published implementation standards, Golden Path CI/CD scaffold, and integrated Veracode SAST/SCA pipeline. Teams use scaffold directly with minimal self-provisioning. |
| Tier 2 | **Conditionally Supported** | Language is approved for documented workload types; no Golden Path CI/CD scaffold is currently published for any language; teams must configure pipeline stages independently; SAST/SCA scanning must be integrated by each team; security scanning is mandatory regardless of scaffold availability |
| Tier 3 | **Requires Architectural Review** | Language is not yet in the documented approved set; or is approved in narrow contexts only; teams must engage the Architecture Review Board before adopting for a new workload; no enterprise Golden Path coverage guaranteed |

**Important**: All languages in the current approved polyglot set are Tier 2 — Conditionally Supported. No language currently has full Golden Path CI/CD scaffold coverage. Teams using any approved language must configure their own pipeline stages and independently integrate Veracode SAST/SCA scanning. C#/.NET gap remediation (standards and Golden Path scaffold) is prioritized for Tier 1 elevation *because* it is the primary enterprise platform — the tooling gaps are largest precisely where the enterprise dependency is deepest. Tier 1 (Fully Supported) will apply when Golden Path scaffolds and implementation standards are published for a language.
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#python]

#### Python

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Governance Tier** | Tier 2 — Conditionally Supported |
| **Version Guidance** | Minimum: Python 3.11; Recommended: Python 3.12 (LTS per [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/)) |
| **Primary Package Manager** | pip with Poetry or pyproject.toml (PEP 517/518 compliant). Note: project-level conventions may further constrain package manager choice within the pip ecosystem (e.g., some projects mandate pip+venv only). |
| **Enterprise Standards** | [STD-TEC-PY-001 through STD-TEC-PY-006](../../../../standards/technology/python/) — fully published |
| **SAST Tooling** | Bandit (security-focused SAST), Ruff (linting + security rules), Veracode (enterprise SAST/SCA) |
| **SCA Tooling** | Veracode SCA; pip-audit for local dependency scanning |
| **Golden Path CI/CD** | ⚠️ Not yet published — teams must configure pipeline stages independently |

**Appropriate Workload Types**

| Workload Type | Fit Assessment | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Data pipelines and ETL | ✅ Primary fit | Pandas, Polars, SQLAlchemy; strong data ecosystem |
| ML/AI model development and experimentation | ✅ Primary fit | PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn; industry-standard tooling |
| Automation scripting and tooling | ✅ Primary fit | Lightweight, rapid development; strong stdlib |
| REST API services (lightweight to moderate scale) | ✅ Appropriate | FastAPI (recommended), Flask, Django REST; not preferred for high-concurrency APIs |
| Integration and orchestration services | ✅ Appropriate | Celery, Kafka consumers, event-driven processing |
| High-concurrency, low-latency APIs | ⚠️ Use with care | Python's GIL limits CPU-bound concurrency; evaluate TypeScript/Node.js or Java instead |
| Frontend UI | ❌ Not applicable | Python does not run in the browser; use TypeScript/JavaScript |

**Strengths (Technical)**

- Extensive data science and ML/AI library ecosystem with no peer in the enterprise stack
- Fast development cycle for scripting, automation, and API prototyping
- Strong AWS SDK and Boto3 support; well-integrated with AWS-native data services (Glue, SageMaker)
- Enterprise SAST/SCA toolchain (Veracode) confirmed available

**Limitations (Technical)**

- GIL constrains CPU-bound multi-threading; not suited for CPU-intensive concurrent workloads without multiprocessing or async patterns
- Dynamic typing increases runtime error risk without strict type annotation enforcement (mypy recommended)
- Dependency management complexity increases with environment size; requires disciplined use of virtual environments or containerization
- Startup time for interpreted runtime can affect cold-start performance in serverless or rapid-scale scenarios

**Version Guidance Source**: [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/) — Python 3.11 reached general availability October 2022; 3.12 reached general availability October 2023. Python maintains a ~5-year security support window per release.

page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#typescript-nodejs]

#### TypeScript (Node.js)

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Governance Tier** | Tier 2 — Conditionally Supported |
| **Version Guidance** | TypeScript: minimum 5.0; Node.js: minimum 20 LTS (Active LTS per [nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases/)) |
| **Primary Package Manager** | npm (v10+) or yarn (v1 stable for Module Federation workloads) |
| **Enterprise Standards** | [STD-TEC-NXT-001 through STD-TEC-NXT-006](../../../../standards/technology/nextjs/) — published for Next.js applications |
| **SAST Tooling** | ESLint (security-focused rule sets), Semgrep, Veracode |
| **SCA Tooling** | Veracode SCA; npm audit for local dependency scanning |
| **Golden Path CI/CD** | ⚠️ Not yet published — teams must configure pipeline stages independently |

**Appropriate Workload Types**

| Workload Type | Fit Assessment | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Micro-frontend applications (React/Next.js) | ✅ Primary fit | Enterprise standard stack; see [GUID-APP-TEC-001](../frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md) for Next.js vs React selection |
| Node.js REST API services | ✅ Primary fit | Express, NestJS; async I/O strength; preferred for JavaScript-ecosystem teams |
| Real-time and event-driven services | ✅ Appropriate | Socket.IO, Kafka consumers; excellent async I/O model |
| BFF (Backend for Frontend) services | ✅ Appropriate | Natural pairing with React micro-frontends; same language across stack |
| CLI tooling and build tooling | ✅ Appropriate | Node.js ecosystem for scaffolding, build scripts, and developer tooling |
| CPU-intensive compute services | ⚠️ Use with care | Node.js event loop is not suited for CPU-bound workloads; evaluate Python or Java |
| ML/AI workloads | ❌ Not the primary fit | Python is the enterprise standard for ML/AI; JavaScript AI libraries lack ecosystem maturity |

**Strengths (Technical)**

- Single language across frontend (React/Next.js) and BFF/API layer reduces cognitive switching for full-stack teams
- Non-blocking async I/O model is well-suited for I/O-intensive API workloads and real-time applications
- TypeScript's static type system catches errors at compile time and improves maintainability over plain JavaScript
- Rich npm ecosystem with strong AWS SDK support

**Limitations (Technical)**

- Node.js event loop architecture is unsuitable for CPU-bound computation without worker threads or offloading
- npm dependency supply chain risk is material; SCA scanning and lockfile governance are required (see Security and Compliance Toolchain section for normative lockfile requirements)
- TypeScript compilation adds a build step; misconfigured `tsconfig.json` can produce less type-safe output than intended
- Module Federation compatibility differences between Next.js and plain React require careful framework selection (see [GUID-APP-TEC-001](../frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md))

**Version Guidance Source**: [nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases/) — Node.js 20 LTS entered Active LTS October 2023; Node.js 22 LTS entered Active LTS October 2024. LTS releases receive security updates for ~3 years.

page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#javascript]

#### JavaScript

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Governance Tier** | Tier 2 — Conditionally Supported |
| **Version Guidance** | ECMAScript 2022 (ES13) minimum target; ES2015 (ES6) as minimum for legacy compatibility where required |
| **Primary Package Manager** | npm |
| **Enterprise Standards** | No dedicated JavaScript-only standard published. TypeScript standards ([STD-TEC-NXT-001](../../../../standards/technology/nextjs/)) apply where TypeScript is used; plain JavaScript guidance is embedded within those standards. |
| **SAST Tooling** | ESLint (security rules), Semgrep, Veracode |
| **SCA Tooling** | Veracode SCA; npm audit |
| **Golden Path CI/CD** | ⚠️ Not yet published — teams must configure pipeline stages independently |

**Appropriate Workload Types**

| Workload Type | Fit Assessment | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy browser scripts (maintenance mode) | ✅ Appropriate | Where TypeScript migration is not yet complete; new code should use TypeScript |
| Build and tooling configuration files | ✅ Appropriate | webpack.config.js, jest.config.js, eslint.config.js; tooling files commonly remain in JS |
| Frontend output bundles | ✅ Appropriate | TypeScript compiles to JavaScript; all browser execution is JavaScript |
| New application development | ⚠️ Prefer TypeScript | New services and applications should use TypeScript over plain JavaScript; JavaScript is conditionally supported for legacy and tooling contexts |
| Backend API services | ⚠️ Prefer TypeScript | TypeScript is strongly preferred for maintainability, type safety, and standards alignment |

**Strengths (Technical)**

- Universal browser runtime; no transpilation required for browser-targeted scripts
- Zero build-time overhead for simple automation and tooling scripts
- Ubiquitous in the npm ecosystem; any Node.js package can be consumed without TypeScript configuration

**Limitations (Technical)**

- No static type checking; runtime type errors are not caught at compile time
- Reduced IDE support and refactoring safety compared to TypeScript
- `any` is the implicit type; larger codebases become difficult to maintain without type annotation discipline
- Security tooling (ESLint security rules) applies equally to JavaScript; lack of types does not reduce SAST requirements

page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#java]

#### Java

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Governance Tier** | Tier 2 — Conditionally Supported |
| **Version Guidance** | Minimum: Java 17 LTS; Recommended: Java 21 LTS (per [adoptium.net/temurin/releases](https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/)) |
| **Primary Package Manager** | Maven or Gradle |
| **Enterprise Standards** | ⚠️ **Gap — Not Yet Published**: Java-specific implementation standards do not currently exist in `standards/technology/`. This is identified as follow-on work. Teams must apply general coding hygiene, SOLID principles ([ADR-APP-001](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-001-design-patterns-languages.md)), and Spring Boot conventions independently until standards are published. |
| **SAST Tooling** | Veracode (SAST/SCA confirmed); SpotBugs / FindBugs with security plugins recommended as developer-side complement |
| **SCA Tooling** | Veracode SCA; OWASP Dependency Check for local scanning |
| **Golden Path CI/CD** | ⚠️ Not yet published — teams must configure pipeline stages independently |

**Appropriate Workload Types**

| Workload Type | Fit Assessment | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise backend services (existing portfolio) | ✅ Primary fit | Significant existing investment; Spring Boot ecosystem; well-supported on AWS EKS |
| High-throughput processing services | ✅ Appropriate | JVM performance characteristics; mature threading model |
| Enterprise integration (ESB patterns, JMS) | ✅ Appropriate | Strong JMS and messaging framework support; Apache Camel |
| Spring Boot microservices | ✅ Appropriate | Standard enterprise Java microservice pattern |
| New greenfield services (Java-skilled teams) | ✅ Appropriate | Valid choice where team skills and ecosystem fit; ensure Veracode scanning is configured |
| ML/AI and data science | ⚠️ Not the primary fit | Python is preferred; Java ML libraries exist but ecosystem maturity is lower |
| Micro-frontend UI development | ❌ Not applicable | Java does not run in the browser; use TypeScript/JavaScript |

**Strengths (Technical)**

- Mature JVM with well-understood performance characteristics for CPU-bound and high-throughput workloads
- Spring Boot provides a comprehensive, battle-tested enterprise application framework
- Strong multi-threading model suitable for CPU-bound concurrent workloads
- Extensive enterprise library ecosystem; well-documented integration patterns
- Strong AWS SDK and EKS support

**Limitations (Technical)**

- JVM startup time can be a constraint for serverless or rapid-scale-to-zero scenarios (GraalVM native image can mitigate but adds build complexity)
- Verbosity of Java code relative to Python or TypeScript increases development time for simple services
- **Enterprise implementation standards not yet published** — teams must apply general guidance independently until standards are available (see gap note above)
- Dependency management (Maven Central / Gradle) requires active SCA scanning for transitive vulnerability exposure

**Version Guidance Source**: [adoptium.net/temurin/releases](https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/) — Eclipse Temurin is the recommended enterprise OpenJDK distribution. Java 17 LTS support extends through September 2029; Java 21 LTS support extends through September 2031.

---
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#c--net]

#### C# / .NET

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Governance Tier** | Tier 2 — Conditionally Supported |
| **Version Guidance** | Minimum: .NET 8 LTS; Recommended: .NET 8 LTS (current LTS per [dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core)) |
| **Primary Package Manager** | NuGet |
| **Enterprise Standards** | ⚠️ **Gap — Highest Priority**: C#/.NET is the primary enterprise language but implementation standards do not yet exist in `standards/technology/`. This is the highest-priority standards gap. Teams must apply general coding hygiene, SOLID principles ([ADR-APP-001](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-001-design-patterns-languages.md)), and ASP.NET Core conventions independently until standards are published. |
| **SAST Tooling** | Veracode (SAST/SCA confirmed); Roslyn analyzers (built into .NET SDK) recommended as developer-side complement |
| **SCA Tooling** | Veracode SCA; `dotnet list package --vulnerable` for local scanning |
| **Golden Path CI/CD** | ⚠️ Not yet published — teams must configure pipeline stages independently (highest priority gap for the primary enterprise language) |

**Appropriate Workload Types**

| Workload Type | Fit Assessment | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise backend services (existing and new) | ✅ Primary fit | Primary enterprise platform; ASP.NET Core is the standard for new API and service development |
| REST API services (ASP.NET Core) | ✅ Primary fit | Enterprise standard for new API development; mature, performant; Swagger/OpenAPI support built in |
| Azure-native applications | ✅ Primary fit | Deep Azure SDK integration; Azure Functions, Service Bus, Cosmos DB native support |
| Windows-integrated workloads | ✅ Appropriate | Where Windows Server dependencies exist; .NET Framework legacy migration targets |
| High-performance compute services | ✅ Appropriate | .NET performance characteristics are competitive with JVM for many workloads |
| ML/AI workloads | ⚠️ Not the primary fit | ML.NET exists but Python is preferred for data science and ML workloads |
| Micro-frontend UI development | ❌ Not applicable | C# Blazor WebAssembly is out of scope for this guidance; TypeScript/JavaScript is the enterprise frontend standard |

**Strengths (Technical)**

- ASP.NET Core delivers competitive performance for REST API workloads
- Strong static typing with modern C# language features (nullable reference types, records, pattern matching)
- Roslyn compiler built-in code analysis provides developer-side security and quality feedback without additional tooling
- Deep Microsoft ecosystem integration (Azure services, SQL Server, Active Directory)
- .NET 8 LTS provides a stable, supported runtime through November 2026

**Limitations (Technical)**

- **Enterprise implementation standards not yet published (highest priority gap)** — C# is the primary enterprise language; teams must apply general guidance independently until standards are available (see gap note above)
- Historically Windows-centric; containerized Linux deployment is fully supported on .NET 6+ but may require attention for teams with older .NET Framework assumptions
- NuGet dependency chain requires active SCA scanning; transitive vulnerability exposure is a documented risk category
- Smaller open-source data science library ecosystem compared to Python

**Version Guidance Source**: [dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core) — .NET 8 LTS is supported through November 2026. **.NET 9 reaches End-of-Life in May 2026 — teams MUST NOT start new projects on .NET 9.** .NET 8 LTS itself expires November 2026; **.NET 10 LTS** (anticipated November 2026) will be the next recommended LTS target. Teams starting new projects now should target .NET 8 LTS and include .NET 10 LTS migration in their product roadmap planning.

[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#known-gaps-and-follow-on-work]

### Known Gaps and Follow-On Work

The following gaps are explicitly documented and require follow-on work. They are not hidden or assumed to be resolved.

| Gap | Description | Impact | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

| Portfolio-wide language usage inventory | Formal discovery of all languages in active use across the portfolio has not been completed | This guidance may not yet reflect all languages in active use | **Open — discovery exercise required** |
| ADR-APP-001 alignment | [ADR-APP-001](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-001-design-patterns-languages.md) is thin and does not reflect the polyglot intent documented here | ADR and this guidance are not fully aligned | **Open — ADR update is follow-on work** |

[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#language-selection-prerequisites]

### Language Selection Prerequisites

Before selecting a language for a new workload, teams should confirm:

1. **Workload type is mapped**: The workload type is listed in the language profile above and the fit assessment is ✅ or ⚠️ (with understanding of the trade-offs)
2. **Governance tier is understood**: The team understands what tooling the enterprise provides and what they must provide themselves
3. **SAST/SCA scanning is planned**: The team has a plan for integrating security scanning into their pipeline before delivery begins
4. **Standards are acknowledged**: Where implementation standards exist, the team is aware of them; where they do not (Java, C#), the team will apply general guidance and SOLID principles
5. **Version guidance is followed**: The team is targeting the minimum supported version or newer, aligned with LTS schedules
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#language-selection-process]

### Language Selection Process

```
Step 1: Identify workload type
  → Data pipeline, ETL, ML/AI
  → REST API service
  → Micro-frontend application
  → Batch processing
  → Automation scripting
  → Enterprise integration

Step 2: Identify candidate languages from workload fit table
  → Filter to languages with ✅ fit for the workload type
  → Note ⚠️ workloads and confirm trade-offs are acceptable

Step 3: Evaluate team skills and ecosystem fit
  → Does the team have active skills in this language?
  → Are dependent systems or libraries primarily in this ecosystem?
  → Does the workload involve integration with existing services in a specific language?

Step 4: Confirm enterprise tooling availability (governance tier)
  → Tier 2 (all current approved languages): Confirm what teams must provide; plan for pipeline configuration; Golden Path scaffolds not yet available
  → Tier 3 / unlisted: Engage Architecture Review Board before proceeding

Step 5: Confirm security scanning plan
  → Identify applicable SAST/SCA tools from the language profile
  → Confirm tools are available in the team's pipeline environment
  → For gaps, engage Platform Engineering before delivery commitment

Step 6: Document the selection
  → For approved language selections (Tier 2): no formal ADR required for using a documented language in its appropriate workload type
  → For new workload contexts not listed in this guidance: document rationale in an ADR
  → For unlisted languages: see Architectural Review Process below
```
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#critical-success-factors]

### Critical Success Factors

- **Engage early**: Language selection is a pre-delivery decision. Discovering tooling gaps after sprint planning begins is avoidable.
- **Read the tier description before the workload fit table**: Understanding what the enterprise provides (or does not) is as important as knowing whether the language fits the workload.
- **Flag gaps to Platform Engineering**: Where SAST/SCA tooling integration instructions are not available, do not skip scanning — engage Platform Engineering to establish coverage before the workload begins.
- **Do not conflate tier with quality**: A Tier 2 language is not a lower-quality choice; it means the team may need to configure more of the pipeline themselves.

[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#workload-to-language-decision-framework]

### Workload-to-Language Decision Framework

The following table provides fit-for-purpose guidance across the primary workload types in the enterprise portfolio. It is a starting point, not a constraint — teams may select among any ✅ languages for a workload based on team skills, ecosystem fit, and existing system context.

| Workload Type | Primary Fit | Also Appropriate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data pipeline / ETL | Python | Java (Spring Batch) | Python's data ecosystem (Pandas, Polars, SQLAlchemy) is the primary fit; Java is appropriate for high-throughput batch with existing JVM infrastructure |
| ML/AI model development | Python | — | Python's library ecosystem (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) has no peer for this workload type in the enterprise stack |
| REST API service — lightweight / moderate scale | C# (ASP.NET Core) | Python (FastAPI), TypeScript (NestJS/Express), Java (Spring Boot) | C# is the enterprise primary for new API development; Python and TypeScript are appropriate where team skills and ecosystem fit |
| REST API service — high-throughput / low-latency | C# (ASP.NET Core) | Java (Spring Boot), TypeScript (NestJS) | .NET performance is well-suited for high-concurrency workloads; Java appropriate for existing Spring Boot investments |
| Micro-frontend application | TypeScript (React / Next.js) | — | TypeScript is the enterprise standard for micro-frontend development; see [GUID-APP-TEC-001](../frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md) |
| BFF (Backend for Frontend) | TypeScript (Node.js) | C# (ASP.NET Core), Python | TypeScript BFF pairs naturally with React/Next.js frontends; C# is appropriate where the team is primarily .NET-based |
| Real-time / event-driven service | TypeScript (Node.js) | Java, Python | Node.js async I/O model is well-suited for event-driven patterns; Java (Kafka, JMS) is appropriate for existing JVM infrastructure |
| Automation scripting | Python | TypeScript (Node.js) | Python is preferred for data-adjacent scripts; Node.js for JavaScript-ecosystem tooling |
| Enterprise integration | C# (.NET), Java (Spring Integration / Camel) | Python | C# preferred for new enterprise integration development; Java appropriate for existing JMS/ESB investments |
| Batch processing | C# (.NET), Java (Spring Batch) | Python | Both .NET and JVM are appropriate for high-throughput batch; C# preferred for new development |
| CLI / build tooling | TypeScript (Node.js) | Python | Node.js is appropriate for JavaScript-ecosystem tooling; Python for data-adjacent scripts and infrastructure automation |

[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#aws-eks-and-container-compatibility]

### AWS EKS and Container Compatibility

All approved languages are deployable as containerized workloads on AWS EKS. The following notes apply:

| Language | Container Notes | AWS SDK Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| Python | Official Python Docker images available; Alpine-based images recommended for production size optimization | Boto3 (AWS SDK for Python) — mature; widely used across enterprise |
| TypeScript (Node.js) | Official Node.js Docker images available; Alpine-based recommended; multi-stage builds for compiled TypeScript | AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 — mature; modular import model reduces bundle size |
| JavaScript | Same as Node.js above | Same as TypeScript above |
| Java | Eclipse Temurin Docker images recommended (Adoptium project); JVM memory tuning required for container environments | AWS SDK for Java 2.x — mature; async HTTP client support |
| C# / .NET | Microsoft .NET Docker images (mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet); multi-stage builds well-supported | AWS SDK for .NET — mature; well-documented |

**Container memory and startup considerations**: JVM (Java) and .NET runtimes have higher baseline memory footprints than interpreted runtimes (Python, Node.js). For workloads with tight memory budgets or rapid scale-to-zero requirements, account for JVM/CLR startup time and baseline heap sizing in infrastructure planning.
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/application/programming-languages/GUID-APP-LANG-001-polyglot-programming-language-guidance.md#security-and-compliance-toolchain]

### Security and Compliance Toolchain

For all approved languages, Veracode SAST/SCA is the enterprise standard scanning platform. The following additional developer-side tools are recommended per language:

| Language | Developer SAST | Developer SCA | Enterprise SAST/SCA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python | Bandit, Ruff | pip-audit | Veracode |
| TypeScript / JavaScript | ESLint (security plugins), Semgrep | npm audit | Veracode |
| Java | SpotBugs + Find Security Bugs plugin | OWASP Dependency Check | Veracode |
| C# / .NET | Roslyn analyzers (built-in), Security Code Scan | `dotnet list package --vulnerable` | Veracode |

**SBOM Generation**: All production workloads MUST generate a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in CycloneDX or SPDX format at minimum per production release. This is a federal compliance obligation per Executive Order 14028 and CMS requirements, not a best practice. See [GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01](../../security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01.md) §SCA Implementation for the authoritative requirement.

**Lockfile Governance**: All production workloads MUST commit the package manager lockfile to version control. Lockfiles MUST be committed atomically with any dependency change. Without committed, pinned dependency manifests, transitive dependency resolution is non-deterministic between CI runs, undermining the SCA coverage mandated above. Required lockfile artifacts per ecosystem:

| Ecosystem | Required Lockfile Artifact |
|---|---|
| npm (TypeScript / JavaScript) | `package-lock.json` |
| pip (Python) | `poetry.lock` or pinned `requirements.txt` |
| Maven / Gradle (Java) | `gradle.lockfile` or Maven dependency locks (`maven-dependency-plugin`) |
| NuGet (C# / .NET) | `packages.lock.json` (SDK-style projects) |

**Veracode Quality Gate Thresholds**: Teams configuring Veracode independently MUST apply the quality gate thresholds defined in [GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01](../../security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01.md) Best Practice 1: fail builds on Critical findings at staging; fail builds on Critical and High findings at production. These thresholds are non-negotiable in Gainwell's HIPAA/FedRAMP environment.

**HIPAA / FedRAMP note**: In Gainwell's regulatory environment, security scanning is not optional at any tier. Where Golden Path pipeline integration instructions are not yet published for a language, teams must integrate Veracode scanning independently. Shipping code without SAST/SCA coverage is not an acceptable trade-off while waiting for Golden Path scaffolding.

### Architectural Review Process for Unsupported Languages

Teams that identify a legitimate workload need that is not well-served by any language in the approved polyglot set must follow this process before adopting the language.

**When ARB review is required**:

- The language is not listed in this guidance document
- The language is listed with a Tier 3 / Requires Review classification (not currently applicable but reserved for future updates)
- A listed language is being used in a workload type where its fit is marked ❌

**When ARB review is NOT required**:

- Choosing between approved languages for a workload where multiple are listed as ✅
- Using an approved (Tier 2) language for a documented workload type (no ARB review, but team must self-provision pipeline configuration and scanning)

**ARB Review Process for Unsupported Languages**:

```
Step 1: Document the business and technical case
  → Why is the workload need not met by any approved language?
  → What specific technical or ecosystem capability is required?
  → What is the estimated scale and longevity of the workload?

Step 2: Complete the following documentation for submission to the ARB:
  → Language name and version
  → Workload type and context
  → Technical rationale for the selection
  → Available SAST/SCA tooling (or plan to establish coverage)
  → Security scanning gap assessment
  → Team skills availability
  → Dependency on any enterprise-unsupported runtime environments

Step 3: Submit to Architecture Review Board
  → Submit via the ADR process ([ADR Development Process](../../../../governance/processes/adr-development.md))
  → ARB reviews against: security toolchain availability, skills availability, runtime supportability, and workload fit

Step 4: Outcomes
  → Approved for this workload: Language is approved for the specific workload context; team provisions their own tooling
  → Approved with conditions: Language is approved with specific constraints (e.g., single workload scope, time-limited)
  → Deferred: Team should re-evaluate an approved language; ARB provides rationale
  → Pathway to Approved Set: ARB identifies requirements for the language to be added to this guidance document
```

**Path to Becoming Enterprise-Supported**

A language may be proposed for addition to the enterprise polyglot set (Tier 1 or Tier 2) when:

- The language has demonstrated active use across multiple teams or workloads
- SAST/SCA toolchain integration with Veracode or an equivalent enterprise scanning platform is confirmed
- Container runtime support on AWS EKS is confirmed
- At least one enterprise architect sponsors the addition
- A minimum set of implementation standards or references (analogous to STD-TEC-PY or STD-TEC-NXT) is drafted or committed

### Compliance Requirements

- All production workloads must have SAST/SCA scanning integrated into their CI/CD pipeline, regardless of language tier
- All production workloads MUST generate an SBOM in CycloneDX or SPDX format per [GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01](../../security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01.md) and Executive Order 14028/CMS requirements
- All production workloads MUST commit the package manager lockfile to version control; lockfiles MUST be committed atomically with any dependency change
- Teams configuring Veracode independently MUST apply the quality gate thresholds defined in [GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01](../../security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-SEC-Testing-2.7.01.md) Best Practice 1 (block Critical at staging; block Critical+High at production)
- Teams using Tier 2 languages must self-provision any pipeline stages not covered by Golden Path templates
- Language selections that deviate from the documented workload fit mappings (e.g., using a language marked ❌ for a workload type) require an ADR and ARB review
- Version guidance must be followed; end-of-life language versions are not permitted in production workloads without an approved exception
